reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that 1 at% Gd micro-alloying improves glass-forming ability in Pd–Ni–P, supporting the premise that a large-atom addition can enhance amorphization via size mismatch. However, the hypothesis applies this to a completely different Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni–P system without direct evidence, and the claim that this will also improve thermal stability during reheating is not addressed in E1.
premises: Gd has a significantly larger atomic radius than the base elements in Pd–Ni–P, increasing atomic size mismatch.
Micro-alloying with ~1 at% Gd can improve glass-forming ability in a metallic glass system.
The effect of Gd on glass formation is noticeable even below 1 at% in the Pd–Ni–P model.
The mechanism of enhanced glass formation is kinetic frustration of crystallization due to atomic size mismatch.
